model.name: Shipment / Consignment
model.purpose: Represent one governed trade shipment or transport consignment, or an explicitly combined logistics view, with goods scope, parties, endpoints, many-to-many allocation, requirements, status assertions and correction lineage without becoming its goods, movement, handling units, documents, trace or fulfilment obligation.
model.scope_statement: Owns mandatory shipment-or-consignment semantic kind; object and revision identity; commercial, carrier, customs and party identifiers; trade and transport party-role bindings; shipment-consignment allocation; item, quantity, value and origin bindings; package, handling-unit and equipment membership references; logistics locations and movement-plan references; service, handling, dangerous-goods, temperature, security, customs and regulatory requirements; planned, estimated, predicted, observed and actual milestone assertions; shipment-scoped custody and responsibility bindings; exceptions and outcome references; qualified measures; document and evidence references; provenance, reconciliation, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Goods, products, orders, contracts, fulfilment, handling units, inventory movements, journeys, routes, services, schedules, parties, places, bookings, transport documents, customs declarations, dangerous-goods masters, sensors, generic events, chain of custody, incidents, insurance claims and evidence masters remain external.
in_scope: Shipment or consignment identity, revision, mandatory semantic kind, party and endpoint boundary, many-to-many allocation and successor lineage
Goods-item scope, package and handling-unit membership references, requirements, movement bindings, milestone assertions, qualified measures and documents
Status, exceptions, responsibility bindings, provenance, reconciliation, privacy, access, retention and interoperability
out_of_scope: Owning goods, products, orders, contracts, fulfilment, handling units, inventory movement, journey, route, service, schedule, party, place, booking, document, declaration, dangerous-goods master, sensor, trace, incident, claim, evidence or payment lifecycles

Equating shipment with consignment, item with package, package with handling unit, custody with ownership, transport status with inventory state, plan with actual movement, milestone assertion with trace event or proof of delivery with fulfilment

Performing transportation, inventory mutation, customs clearance, dangerous-goods certification, custody proof, claims determination, autonomous consequential rerouting, protected disclosure or irreversible deletion

boundary_notes.distinction: Goods Movement / Logistics is a broader flow context. Shipment / Consignment owns the bounded trade or transport grouping and its assertions; the registered parent signal remains candidate until both models are jointly reviewed.

Shipment / Consignment records membership, loading, marks and seals. Handling-unit identity, physical properties, nesting, condition and lifecycle remain externally mastered; CONTAINS is accepted only as typed membership.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-FLW-009 Journey / Trip and WM-FLW-010 Route / Itinerary
boundary_notes.distinction: Shipment / Consignment binds planned or actual transport references and milestones. Journey execution, route geometry, movement observations and outcomes remain externally mastered.
A shipment milestone may cause or correlate with inventory movement, but stock ledger, location balance, reservation and inventory adjustment remain Inventory Movement concerns.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-FLW-013 Supply-chain Trace / Chain of Custody
boundary_notes.distinction: The model binds source-qualified milestones and current custody or responsibility assertions. Cross-organizational event graph, chain-of-custody proof and trace-query lifecycle remain in the trace pattern.
Fulfilment may reference shipments as physical delivery evidence. Commercial obligation, acceptance, proof evaluation, remedies and fulfilment outcome remain externally mastered.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Transport document, Customs declaration and Insurance claim
boundary_notes.distinction: Shipping instructions, waybills, bills of lading, declarations and claims are independently governed records referenced by the shipment or consignment; their issuance, legal effect and adjudication are external.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the Dimension owner, shipment and consignment stewards, trade and transport authorities and accountable decision roles.

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint shipment, consignment, revision, allocation, item-binding, milestone-assertion, exception and projection identifiers only in the adopting Dimension namespace; preserve external master identities as typed references.
registry_links: Dimension-local shipment, consignment, allocation, identifier, status, access, retention and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, mandatory semantic kind, authoritative master ID, immutable revision, party and endpoint boundary, item scope and source profile; never use date, tracking number, document number, barcode, endpoint pair or hash alone as identity.

Keep trade shipment, transport consignment, goods item, consignment item, package, handling unit, transport equipment, inventory movement, journey, trace event, delivery obligation and transport document distinct and preserve allocations, corrections and successors.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare target node, trade, mode or jurisdiction profile, authority, source, rationale, access, time and interoperability impact.
Breaking changes require a new version, migration and crosswalk maps, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior object revisions, allocations and identifiers.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when kind, identity, item allocation, parties, endpoints, clocks, status, authority, provenance and access meaning remain intact.
UN/CEFACT, WCO, UBL, GS1, IATA, DCSA, eFTI, UN/LOCODE, units and provenance mappings pin source and target versions and declare transformed, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative shipment or consignment master-system identifier and immutable revision.
Governed globally resolvable shipment, consignment, allocation or milestone IRI.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep planned, estimated, predicted, observed, actual, record, correction and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {shipment-or-consignment-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-event-id}; never use a date, tracking code, document number, barcode, party, location, filename or hash alone as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, source and vocabulary versions, object scope, event and record times, provenance, assurance, license and access marking for each retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may create, allocate, compose, bind, instruct, assert status, correct, disclose, retain and tombstone shipment or consignment records.

Every assertion requires mandatory semantic kind, identity and revision, item or logistics scope, party and endpoint context, time kind, source, authority, confidence, status and lineage as applicable.

Agents never infer ownership, custody, fulfilment, inventory state, legal permission, customs clearance, safe handling, delivery completion or claim validity from a status, tracking code, document or location alone.

Goods, orders, fulfilment, handling units, inventory movements, journeys, routes, services, parties, locations, contracts, bookings, documents, declarations, dangerous-goods masters, sensors, trace, incidents, claims and evidence remain external masters.

Automated agents may append low-risk memberships, status assertions, reconciliations and projections under delegation, but custody transfer, customs declaration, dangerous-goods decisions, protected disclosure and irreversible deletion require accountable authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, mandatory kind, requested revision, item scope, status horizon, assurance, freshness, license and access policy; return the minimum permitted projection.
create: Create stable identity, mandatory kind, party and endpoint boundary, item scope, source, authority and explicit unknowns before adding allocations, units or milestone assertions.
update: Append an immutable allocation, composition, instruction, status, measurement, exception or correction revision with actor, authority, reason, RFC 3339 effective time and predecessor.
delete: Apply trade, customs, safety, dispute, audit, retention, disposition and legal-hold policy; tombstone eligible Shipment / Consignment-owned records or withdraw projections while preserving identity, material provenance and non-cascading external references. The adopting Dimension policy owns execution.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and sensitive disclosure unless the active Dimension, role, purpose, object kind, trade confidentiality, location sensitivity, customs or safety rule, license and field policy grant the action; expose the minimum necessary projection.
exceptions: Emergency or regulatory access must be legally grounded, time-limited, purpose-bound, attributable, independently reviewed and unable to erase immutable shipment, consignment, correction or legal-hold evidence.
audit_requirements: Log actor, role, purpose, object and revision identity, action, decision, policy and vocabulary versions, RFC 3339 timestamp with offset, affected fields, source evidence and outcome for privileged mutation or disclosure.

Read this model AGENTS.md, pinned spec.yaml and required goods, order, handling-unit, inventory, journey, route, service, party, location, contract, booking, document, declaration, dangerous-goods, trace, sensor, incident, claim and evidence model instructions before mutation.

checklist.notes: Trade shipment, transport consignment, revision, allocation, item binding, milestone assertion and projection identities remain distinct.
Mandatory kind separates seller-to-buyer goods grouping from consignor-to-consignee transport-contract grouping.
Party and endpoint boundary, item scope, requirements, qualified measures and status assertions are covered without importing external masters.
Master assertion, plan, prediction, status report, EPCIS event, sensor observation, document and correction are distinguished.
Draft, planned, booked, accepted, picked-up, in-transit, arrived, delivered, returned, cancelled, corrected and tombstoned states preserve history.
Trade and transport parties, goods, packages, handling units, journeys, routes, services, documents, declarations, trace and claims use typed bindings.
Planned, estimated, predicted, observed, actual, record, correction and ingestion clocks remain distinct.
Origin, destination, receipt, loading, transshipment, unloading, border, storage and delivery location functions are explicit.
Sources, actors, methods, documents, events, derivations, revisions and invalidations are linked.
Trade ownership, custody, possession, control, risk, responsibility and data mastership are not conflated.
Identity, kind, many-to-many allocation, quantity balance, membership, endpoint, clock, requirement, measurement, document and crosswalk checks are explicit.
Role, purpose, commercial confidentiality, customs, safety, location sensitivity, minimum projection and audit are represented.
Corrections, disputes, customs or legal hold, withdrawal and tombstones are explicit and non-cascading.
UN/CEFACT, WCO, UBL, GS1, IATA, DCSA, eFTI, UN/LOCODE, ISO, RFC, PROV, DQV and ODRL mappings disclose loss.
Registration, allocation, item composition, unit binding, movement binding, requirements, milestones, exceptions, reconciliation and projection declare controlled effects.

known_omissions: Trade, mode, region, customs, dangerous-goods, security, temperature, food, pharmaceutical, animal, waste, sanctions, export-control, safety, privacy, licensing and retention profiles require exact current rules and competent review.

Goods, orders, contracts, fulfilment, handling units, inventory, journeys, routes, services, bookings, documents, declarations, dangerous-goods masters, trace, sensors, incidents, claims and evidence lifecycles remain in neighboring models.
Certified field crosswalks, status inference, ETA, exception causality, custody proof, customs admissibility and legal evidence requirements remain future work.
conflicts: UN/CEFACT and WCO use shipment as the trade or goods view and consignment as the transport-contract view, while UBL describes them as contractual or logical versus physical or logistical views; the model requires a mandatory semantic kind and source profile.
Shipment and consignment have many-to-many allocation under split and consolidated transport, so neither can be treated as the universal container of the other.

A tracking status, EPCIS event, sensor reading, transport document, customs declaration and proof of delivery are different assertion or evidence classes and cannot silently establish ownership, custody, fulfilment or legal clearance.
regional_assumptions: WCO customs guidance and EU eFTI rules are regulatory profiles rather than universal commercial or transport law.
IATA ONE Record and DCSA Track and Trace are modal profiles for air cargo and container shipping and do not define all shipment types.
Dangerous-goods, customs, sanctions, transport documents, title, custody and delivery consequences depend on mode, contract and jurisdiction.
adversarial_checks: Reject an object without stable identity, mandatory shipment-or-consignment kind, revision, party and endpoint boundary, item scope, source and lineage.
Reject shipment and consignment collapsed into one identity or a one-to-many-only relationship that cannot represent split and consolidated transport.
Reject a goods item, package, handling unit, container, inventory movement, journey, status event, document or delivery obligation represented as the shipment or consignment itself.
Reject planned, estimated, predicted, observed and actual milestone times collapsed into one timestamp or interpreted without source and timezone rules.
Reject custody, ownership, fulfilment, customs clearance, safe condition or delivery inferred from location, tracking status, waybill or proof label alone.
Reject last-write-wins when item quantities, handling-unit membership, status assertions, measurements or documents conflict; preserve source, clocks, correction and precedence.
Reject protected commercial or location disclosure, dangerous-goods decision, customs submission or record destruction outside delegated authority.
